title: oncall-handoff-temp-runbook-priya-menon
content:
Purpose: quick handoff + temporary procedures for Priya's oncall shift. Mostly notes & TODOs - not final.

SHIFT SUMMARY (brief)
- Time window: 2026-02-27 17:00 -> 2026-02-28 01:00 PT (local).
- Overall cluster health: green, one transient spike in p50/p95 on us-west-2 dedicated pool around 22:10.
- Incidents: 1x degraded-throughput (RDMFR-4712) that was mitigated with a rollout rollback + cache flush.
- Follow-ups: root cause investigation (ticket linked), short-term mitigation validated, long-term fix planned.

WHAT HAPPENED (brief chronology)
- 21:55: SLO alert fired: dedicated-us-west-2 throughput drop > 30% for 5m. Alert title: "dedicated-usw2-throughput-degradation". Pager to eng-sre on-call.
- 22:00: Checked console -> many inferences queuing on a small subset of instances (pool imbalance).
- 22:05: Noticed elevated kernel OOM logs on a subset of nodes (nv-kernel OOM entries). Linked logs: /var/log/serving-runtime/nv-kernel.log (see grep nv_oom).
- 22:12: Quick mitigation: rolled back serving-runtime rollout to v3.9.1-stable (previous candidate v3.10.0-rc had a change to kernel selection heuristics).
- 22:18: Flushed prefix KV cache for affected model group (model: redwood-open-7b-quant) to avoid hot-KV pressure (console -> model -> cache -> flush).
- 22:25: Throughput recovered to normal; p95 back within SLO. Alerts auto-resolved.

TEMPORARY PROCEDURES (for this shift)
- If p50/p95 latency increase and queue length > 2000 per instance group:
  1) Check dedicated pool balance: Console -> Dedicated -> Pools -> us-west-2 -> instance distribution. If imbalance, trigger manual rebalance (button in console) OR scale up by +2 nodes (if autoscale not responding).
  2) If kernel OOM entries present (grep nv_oom on /var/log/serving-runtime/*), rollback recent rollout: ops steps: Console -> Rollouts -> select model-serving rollout -> rollback to last stable (note stable tag in PR description).
  3) Flush KV cache for model group: Console -> Models -> {model} -> Cache -> Flush prefix cache. This prevents KV hotness while we stabilize.
  4) If memory/cuda errors persist after rollback, isolate nodes by cordon + drain: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; notify infra.

- Emergency contact order: (1) oncall infra (Evan Brooks), (2) serving-runtime lead (Maya Singh), (3) SRE manager (Samir Ali). Slack channel: #oncall-redwood (use @here sparingly). Pager escalation: follow escalation policy in Confluence (link above).

CHECKLIST (first 10m)
- [ ] Confirm alert details (pager + console alert).
- [ ] Identify affected pool(s) and models.
- [ ] Check instance metrics: GPU mem, CUDA errors, CPU steal, disk IO.
- [ ] Check recent rollouts (past 24h) and PRs merged into serving-runtime (look for kernel selection / caching changes).
- [ ] If immediate mitigation needed: rollback -> flush cache -> rebalance/scale.

COMMON COMMANDS / LOG PATHS
- Tail runtime logs on node: sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -f
- GPU kernel OOMs: sudo cat /var/log/serving-runtime/nv-kernel.log | tail -n 500 | grep -i oom
- List recent rollouts: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts?env=prod
- Flush cache via admin API: POST /api/models/{model}/cache/flush with admin token (standard header).

OBSERVABILITY (where to look)
- Console Dashboards:
  - overall: Console -> Observability -> Token-level latency (p50/p95)
  - model: Console -> Models -> redwood-open-7b-quant -> Metrics
  - dedicated pool: Console -> Dedicated -> us-west-2 -> Pool metrics (GPU mem, queue length)
- Grafana: grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving-runtime/summary
- Traces: Jaeger service: traces.redwood.ai -> service=serving-runtime -> look for long tail spans in KV access codepath.

KNOWN WORKAROUNDS (temporary)
- If KV hotness suspected: flush model prefix cache + enable short-lived per-request cache TTL (set in model config via console) to 5s until root cause fixed.
- If specific instance shows repeated OOMs: isolate and replace (cordon/drain).

UNRESOLVED / TODO (follow-ups for next rotations)
- RDMFR-4712: full RCA required - suspected kernel selection heuristics change in v3.10.0-rc; need reproducer and perf test. Assigned to Maya (see JIRA).
- Add automated rollback-trigger playbook if throughput drops >40% for 10m. (PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982)
- Add healthcheck to detect KV hot prefixes and auto-shed or throttle.
- Update permanent runbook with exact CLI snippets and required roles/permissions for cache flush and rollbacks (current steps are scattered).

NOTES TO SELF (short)
- Need to capture exact kernel OOM log lines next time - current grep is noisy. Consider adding structured logging for nv-kernel.
- Remember to update incident timeline in Confluence before EOD.

QUICK LINKS
- Incident ticket: JIRA-RDMFR-4712 (investigation + timeline)
- Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982
- Confluence incident page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RDMFR-4712
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01SERV/psg12345

STYLE / PRIVACY
- This doc is for internal oncall use only; do not copy external-facing content until incident summary is sanitized.

END (temporary runbook draft)

-- Priya
